headline: US stocks reopen for a half day (1 p.m. ET close) after Thanksgiving. Futures point higher as chip stocks rebounded in Asia after Wednesday's rout. 10-year yield back above 4.9%, a Dec 9 Fed hike near certain. Oil up about 3% on Middle East attacks. New US tariffs on many partners.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. A 25 bp Fed hike at the 8-9 December meeting is priced as near certain after October core PCE of 3.3%, a mild headwind already expected.
No specific US telecom news. The 10-year yield climbed back above 4.9% on Friday after a two-month low Wednesday, which takes back a little of the help for dividend payers.
A December Fed hike is about fully priced, keeping loan costs high, and the new tariff round includes a 15% levy on Japanese exports such as cars, which Japan has protested.
Defensive names have no clear month-long driver. The new tariffs could raise some input costs, but money is rotating back toward tech as fear eases.
Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% and the economy looks resilient, a plus, but hot inflation and a near-certain December hike limit the upside.
New US tariffs on China, the EU and about a dozen other economies could raise import costs, but final effects and timing are still unclear. No clear direction.

Chips rebounded overseas after Wednesday's rout (Nasdaq briefly down 4.6% intraday), with Kioxia, SK Hynix and Tokyo Electron higher and US futures up. But AI nerves and Nvidia governance worries remain, so no clear month view.
US crude rose about 3% to near $86 and Brent is above $95 after attacks on Saudi oil facilities and Strait of Hormuz shipping risks. A tailwind if prices hold, but oil swings fast.
A December hike and a 10-year near 4.9% can help bank lending margins, but higher rates also slow borrowing and markets were very volatile this week. No clear direction.

Mixed: gold rebounded about 2% to near $3,650 from a 15-month low and silver jumped, but copper is down about 17% in November, one of its worst months in over a decade.
Higher oil raises feedstock costs and new tariffs add uncertainty, but no clear sector-specific news.
New tariffs on many trading partners could help some US makers and hurt others that import parts. Strong Q3 GDP helps demand. No clear direction.
Black Friday spending results are not out yet. Tariffs on imports and a near-certain December hike are headwinds, but the economy still looks resilient.
AI stocks rebounded overseas and Nasdaq futures are higher, but investors remain cautious about the AI trade after Wednesday's sharp intraday drop.
US crude rose about 3% to near $86 on Middle East supply worries, raising fuel costs for airlines and truckers, and new tariffs may weigh on trade volumes.
The 10-year yield rose back above 4.9% and a December hike is priced in, a mild headwind for rate-sensitive utilities, but they stay a defensive place in volatile markets.

avoid.NVDA: S&P Global Ratings warned on 25 Nov it could downgrade Nvidia's credit over management and governance concerns, after a steep November fall; very volatile for a month-long hold.
